items.note: The table filter field takes a 2px blue focus border on its pill shape, with a clear button. The table narrows to one row and the 'showing 1 of 8' count updates. This is clean, and it follows the reference's form controls and its blue focus colour (09, 11). The earlier 'focused field keeps its resting border' gap is closed.

At night the focused filter pill gets a yellow ring on the indigo field, and the table filters to one row. This is the night palette with a clearly visible focus colour, in step with the reference's navy/indigo treatment (03).

On the phone the filter field spans the full width with a blue focus border and a clear button. The one-row table scrolls in its frame and the chip strip scrolls sideways. Clear and in the system's language. The stacked nav, search and avatar rows still push content below the first screen.

The table is well built: 1px rules, bold underlined project titles, small status tags with dots and right-aligned budgets. No hovered row is visible, though, because every row has the same white fill. The reference's interactive rows show a clear state change (05, 10).
The night table is navy with indigo rules and the status tags still read. As in light, no row looks hovered, so the state cannot be read from the screen.

On the phone the table shows only the project and owner columns in a scrolling frame, and owner names wrap to two lines. No row shows a hover or press state. The rest is tidy and in the system's language.

The focused sidebar nav item gets a full pill-shaped 2px blue ring that follows the item's shape. It sits next to the ink 'selected' pill with its white dot. This matches the reference's ring on its pills (11) and closes the earlier 'flush square outline' gap.
At night the focused nav pill gets a yellow ring on the indigo sidebar, with the white selected pill above it. It is clearly visible and in the system's language.
In the phone's top nav strip the focused item gets a pill ring that is not clipped. It sits beside the ink selected pill with its dot. It reads clearly, close to the reference's pill-tab row (09).

The account chip darkens a step, and a white rounded menu with the float shadow drops below it: the email in label grey, then three plain items. It is quiet and correct, in line with the spec's menu treatment. It is a little plain, because no rule or tone sets the sign-out item apart.
At night the menu is an indigo panel under the indigo account chip, with white items. It is consistent with the night palette and easy to read.
On the phone the menu is a wide white rounded panel with the float shadow under the avatar circle, with large touch rows. It covers the page heading cleanly with no clipping.

The empty state has a blue zigzag glyph, a bold h4 title, one line of help and an ink 'clear' pill, so it reads clearly. It sits in a white box with a grey border inside the cream panel, with a lot of empty space around a small glyph. The reference never borders its cards and fills space with tone and composed shapes.

At night it is the same bordered navy box inside the indigo panel, with the blue zigzag, title, help line and a white pill. It is clear, but it is the same bordered card where the system calls for a toned panel.

On the phone the bordered white box sits below the full-width focused filter, with the zigzag glyph, a two-line title and an ink pill. It reads well, with the same bordered-card treatment as on desktop.

The stat tiles turn into cream skeletons, each with pop dots and a 'Loading' label. The refresh pill keeps its width and shows the pop dots. This follows the spec and fixes the earlier 'no loading text' gap, though the saturated tiles going cream loses colour for a moment.
At night the skeletons are indigo, with pop dots and 'Loading' text, and the white pill holds its pop dots. It is consistent with light mode and clear.
On the phone the full-width ink pill shows centred pop dots, and four cream skeleton tiles each carry 'Loading' and two skeleton bars. It reads clearly and in the system's language.

The greeting glyph is a crescent-shaded yellow disc with a tucked orange sparkle. The four stat-tile plates hold distinct, readable pictograms: a rocket, a clock, a rain cloud and a calendar, each with a sparkle. The flat crescent-shaded style is close to the reference's spot plates (07). Some pictograms fill a little under the 60–70% of the plate.

The blue header band holds a tight cluster: a large yolk disc with a darker crescent, a white flat-bottomed cloud overlapping its edge, and a pink four-point sparkle. It is built to the recipe and much closer to the reference's cloud-and-sparkle compositions (02) than the scattered stickers of the earlier round.

The detail page's blue band repeats the projects cluster, which is fair because it is the same area. Its cover is a crescent-shaded pink rocket with orange fins and a sparkle on a blue panel: readable and well crafted. The rocket also repeats the stat-tile pictogram.

The green band's cluster is a different layout: a pink blob with a crescent, an orange pill tucked under its left edge and a white sparkle. Avatars are flat, slightly shaded discs with initials. This varies per area as the spec asks and stays flat and face-free like the reference (06).

The greeting glyph breathes on a slow 6s loop with gentle scale and rotation. Stat-tile plates and the detail cover fade in once over 500ms, with no travel and no bounce. This matches the spec's calm Breathing and Reveal patterns, and the earlier build-on-view live list is gone.

findings.summary: Data-table rows show no visible hover: a hovered row looks the same as its neighbours in light, dark and phone layouts. The reference's interactive rows and pills always show a clear state change.

The filtered-empty state is a white box with a grey border inside the cream panel, and its small glyph floats in a lot of space. The reference never borders cards: it separates layers by tone and fills a state's space with a composed shape group or a large glyph.
